d.d: The amount of time that some being has been alive, or that some thing has been in existence, as measured from its birth or origin until the present or until some other given reference point. (Often measured in number of years; alternatively in months, days, hours, etc.; see also the usage notes)
d.x: "What is the age of your oldest child?" — "He's ten." (ten years old)

d.d: The state of being old; the latter part of life.
d.x: Wisdom doesn't necessarily come with age, sometimes age just shows up all by itself.

d.d: Any particular stage of life.
To grow aged; to become old or older; to show marks of age.
d.x: He grew fat as he aged.

d.d: To suffer the passage of time so as to later be viewed or turn out in a certain way.
d.x: His prediction that we didn't stand a chance hasn't aged well, now that we've won the cup.

d.d: To cause to grow old; to impart the characteristics of age to.
Old.

d.d: Having undergone the improving effects of time; matured.
Old people, collectively.

d.d: Having existed for so great a period of time that its longevity cannot be expressed.
d.x: The ageless pyramids stood prominently against the sunset.

d.d: Continuing infinitely or indefinitely.
d.x: This memorial will show our ageless respect to those who died.

d.d: Always appearing youthful; never seeming to age.
